title: LP2-00–55: two known Vigenère keys and nine openings

reader_test.input: Archived rune text from LP2-00 through LP2-55, including headings, and the two previously known keys of 8 and 13 runes.
reader_test.action: Repeat each key from every starting place in its cycle, trying addition and subtraction and restarting independently on each page.
reader_test.check: A candidate passes only if its first 12 output runes exactly match the beginning of one of nine fixed known readings.

question: Do either of the two known Vigenere keys recover a 12-rune known-reading opening at the start of an LP2-00–55 page under uninterrupted repeating-key decoding?
summary: All 2352 key/phase/direction/page cases completed. None matched the first 12 runes of any of the nine declared known openings. Other keys, plaintext beginnings and interruption rules remain untested.

scope.representation: Complete archived rune stream including headings; remove non-alphabet characters; no corrections or reversal.
scope.procedure: Apply each known key with every phase, both addition and subtraction modulo 29. Compare the first 12 output indices against each of nine known-opening vectors. Retain complete candidates.
scope.parameters: Two vectors of lengths 8 and 13; all 21 phases; two signs; 56 pages; 2352 candidates and 21168 exact comparisons. Reset per page. No interruptions.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, interruption placement, noninitial positions, heading removal, cross-page carry, alternative alphabets, transposition and language scoring.

finding: Zero matching cases among 2352 completed candidates, with 21168 exact opening comparisons. The separate checker and full rerun reproduce every sequence and decision.
limitations: Only two key vectors and nine fixed initial openings. A valid plaintext may begin differently. No language score, interruption search, or claim against Vigenère in general. Computational review only; human review pending.
next_steps: For phase-zero second-koan subtraction and the fixed Warning opening, a mismatch-before-reset proof rules out all 55 line-reset page starts and 54 word-reset starts. Only LP2-54 needs the declared word-reset check. Other keys, phases, beginnings and interruption rules require separately bounded tests.

family.title: Reuse of known repeating keys
family.question: Do specified known key vectors recover explicitly declared openings under fixed alignment rules?

variant.label: Baseline: two keys, all phases, no interruptions

review.reviewer: Codex — full rerun, opening controls and independent iterator check; human review pending

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.10, standard library. Independent verification: python experiments/records/lp2-known-vigenere-keys/check.py

visuals.caption: The exact search space: two known keys, all phases, both arithmetic directions, 56 pages, and nine fixed openings. No opening matches occurred; other plaintext beginnings remain outside this test.

reader_finding: The Welcome and second-koan keys did not recover any of nine known 12-rune openings. Every starting position in each key and both addition and subtraction were tested.
reader_limit: The keys ran continuously and restarted on each page. Other keys, pauses or skips in the key, and different beginnings remain untested.

browser_followups.motivation: A key is a list of shifts through the rune alphabet. Subtract the 13-number pattern used to decode the second koan, starting it again at each word instead of continuing through the page. On LP2-54, check whether the first 12 outputs match Warning, an already decoded passage.
browser_followups.title: Restart a known 13-number shift pattern at each word
browser_followups.question: Does repeating the second-koan key from its first rune at every transcription word recover the fixed 12-rune Warning opening at a page start?
browser_followups.scope_change: Only LP2-54 remains eligible: on the other 54 rune pages, the saved page-reset output already disagrees with the Warning opening before a word reset could change anything. This checks the remaining page with one key, subtraction and phase zero.
browser_followups.limitation: A match establishes only compatibility with this 12-rune beginning, not a complete reading. Every non-rune ends a transcription word; headings remain included. No skips, later offsets, alternative phases or other openings are tested. Surviving the prefix check does not mean LP2-54 is a match.

value.detail: Test only the fixed 12-rune Warning opening under the declared second-koan word-reset hypothesis; a match is not a complete decipherment.
